cards.name: Keep a headache diary

says.text: Keep the diary for at least 8 weeks, writing down how often headaches come, how long they last and how bad they are, anything that comes with them, every medicine taken for them (prescribed or bought), what may have set them off, and how they fall against periods.
A diary can show how often, how long and how bad headaches are, whether a treatment is helping, and give the person and their clinician something to talk through.
Characterization of frequently recurring headache generally requires a headache diary to record information on pain and associated symptoms day-by-day for at least one month.
It can help to keep a migraine diary to help you work out what might trigger your migraine attacks.

sources.title: Headaches in over 12s: diagnosis and management (CG150)

checks.label: Days since the diary was started
checks.basis: NICE CG150 1.1.4: at least 8 weeks

not_said: A diary does not diagnose. NICE asks a clinician to read it with the person.

cards.name: Painkiller days

says.text: Clinicians should think of medication overuse headache when a headache began or got worse while someone took triptans, opioids, ergots or combination painkillers on 10 or more days a month, or paracetamol, aspirin or an NSAID on 15 or more days a month, for 3 months or longer.
People taking medicines for headaches should be told about the risk of medication overuse headache.
Try not to take painkillers for more than 2 days a week as this can cause you to get more headaches and make migraine harder to treat.
…based on expert opinion rather than on formal evidence.

sources.title: Headaches in over 12s: diagnosis and management (CG150)

choose.label: Paracetamol, aspirin or an NSAID (such as ibuprofen)
A triptan, an opioid, an ergot, or a combination painkiller

checks.label: Days this week with any painkiller
checks.basis: NHS: "more than 2 days a week"

checks.label: Days this month with paracetamol, aspirin or an NSAID
checks.basis: NICE CG150 1.2.7: 15 or more days a month, for 3 months or longer

checks.label: Days this month with a triptan, opioid, ergot or combination
checks.basis: NICE CG150 1.2.7: 10 or more days a month, for 3 months or longer

not_said: It does not say you have medication overuse headache: NICE also asks whether the headache developed or worsened while taking them, for 3 months or more.
It does not tell you to stop a medicine. That is for a clinician, after a diagnosis.
Which class a medicine is in is your choice when you follow this card; the app does not work it out from a name.

cards.name: Fewer dust mites in the bedroom

says.text: Trials to date have on the whole been small and of poor methodological quality, making it difficult to offer any definitive recommendations on the role, if any, of house dust mite avoidance measures…

…acaricides and extensive bedroom-based environmental control programmes may be of some benefit in reducing rhinitis symptoms. Isolated use of house dust mite impermeable bedding is unlikely to prove effective.

says.by: Cochrane review CD001187 (Gøtzsche and Johansen), on asthma
says.text: Chemical and physical methods aimed at reducing exposure to house dust mite allergens cannot be recommended.
This 2011 review predates current reporting standards and methodological expectations for Cochrane Reviews. It should not be used for clinical decision‐making.
Bedding should be washed weekly in hot water (130° F) and dried in a hot dryer.

says.by: Choi et al. 2008, a laboratory laundry test
says.text: Using the 30 degrees C and 40 degrees C washing modes, only 6.5% and 9.6% of Dermatophagoides farinae, respectively, were killed. However, using the 60 degrees C and SW washing modes, all HDMs were killed.

cards.disagree: A Cambridge University Hospitals NHS leaflet calls allergy covers "the single most effective measure but is not enough to help on its own"; Cochrane found covers on their own "unlikely to prove effective". Each is shown with its name.

sources.title: House dust mite avoidance measures for perennial allergic rhinitis (CD001563)
House dust mite control measures for asthma (CD001187)

sources.by: Choi et al., Ann Allergy Asthma Immunol 2008
sources.title: Removal of house dust mite, dog dander and pollen allergens in mechanical laundry

checks.label: Days this week the bedding was washed
checks.basis: AAAAI: "washed weekly in hot water (130° F)"

checks.label: Washes this week at 60 °C or more
checks.basis: Choi 2008, a laboratory test: "using the 60 degrees C … all HDMs were killed"

not_said: It does not say these measures relieve symptoms: the reviews found the evidence weak for rhinitis and no effect in asthma.
It does not say that 54 °C, AAAAI's 130 °F, kills every mite; only 60 °C was tested.

cards.name: Rinsing the nose with salt water

says.text: Saline irrigation may reduce patient-reported disease severity compared with no saline irrigation at up to three months in both adults and children with allergic rhinitis, with no reported adverse effects.
The overall quality of evidence was low or very low.
Repeat the first 5 steps up to 3 times a day (making a new solution each time) until your nose feels more comfortable.

checks.label: Days this week with more than 3 rinses
checks.basis: NHS: "up to 3 times a day"

not_said: No data were available beyond three months.
It is uncertain whether rinsing helps on top of medicines, and there is not enough evidence to compare it with steroid sprays.

cards.name: Hay fever self-care

says.text: shower and change your clothes after you have been outside to wash pollen off
keep windows and doors shut as much as possible
vacuum regularly and dust with a damp cloth
do not smoke or be around smoke – it makes your symptoms worse
do not dry clothes outside – they can catch pollen
…they should not be used for longer than 5 days as this can make a blocked nose worse

checks.label: Most days in a row with a decongestant spray, last 30 days
checks.basis: NHS, on decongestants: "should not be used for longer than 5 days"

not_said: The NHS page cites no trials for these measures; none of them is shown here as proven.

cards.name: When to see someone

urgent.text: Call 999 or go to A&E if: You or a child has a headache and: has had a seizure (fit) / has numbness or weakness in the body or face / it started suddenly and is extremely painful / has had a head injury within the last 3 months / are finding it difficult to speak, balance, walk or remember things / are drowsy or confused / has loss of vision / has a rash that does not fade when a glass is rolled over it / has a very high temperature, a stiff neck, or bright lights are bothering you

says.text: See a GP if: you have allergic rhinitis and your symptoms get worse / you also have asthma and it's getting worse / your symptoms are affecting your sleep and everyday life / you're not sure what's causing your symptoms / treatments from a pharmacist are not working
you have migraine attacks more than once a week
not getting better or is getting worse / you regularly get headaches

says.by: ARIA pharmacy guide (Lourenço et al. 2020, CC BY 4.0)
says.text: Patients presenting with unilateral symptoms, recurrent nasal bleeding, clear rhinorrhea which is largely unilateral and worse on bending forward, or purulent rhinorrhea, especially if accompanied with fever, should be referred to a physician

not_said: No source gives a number for these, so the app counts nothing here.
999 is the UK's emergency number. Where you live, use your own.

cards.name: Sleep

says.text: Adults should sleep 7 or more hours per night on a regular basis to promote optimal health.
…to promote optimal health among adults aged 18 to 60 years.

Sleeping more than 9 hours per night on a regular basis may be appropriate for young adults, individuals recovering from sleep debt, and individuals with illnesses. For others, it is uncertain whether sleeping more than 9 hours per night is associated with health risk.
People concerned they are sleeping too little or too much should consult their healthcare provider.

sources.title: Recommended amount of sleep for a healthy adult (J Clin Sleep Med 2015)

checks.label: Nights this week of 7 hours or more
checks.basis: AASM and SRS: "7 or more hours per night on a regular basis", for adults aged 18 to 60

not_said: It does not call more than 9 hours harmful: the source says it is uncertain.
For other ages the CDC gives 61–64: 7–9 hours, and 65 and over: 7–8 hours.

cards.name: Caffeine

says.text: Intakes up to 400mg per day (about 5.7mg/kg bw per day) consumed throughout the day do not raise safety concerns for healthy adults in the general population, except pregnant women.
Caffeine intakes from all sources up to 200mg per day consumed throughout the day do not raise safety concerns for the foetus.
Single doses of 100mg (about 1.4mg/kg bw) of caffeine may affect sleep duration and patterns in some adults, particularly when consumed close to bedtime.
too much caffeine

checks.label: Days this week over 400 mg
checks.basis: EFSA: "up to 400mg per day … do not raise safety concerns for healthy adults", except in pregnancy (200 mg)

not_said: 400 mg is not a target.
The app does not work out milligrams from cups; you write the milligrams.

cards.name: Water

says.text: Adequate total water intakes for females would have to be 2.0 L/day (95th percentile 3.1 L) and for males 2.5 L/day (95th percentile 4.0 L).
…reference values for total water intake should include water from drinking water, beverages of all kind, and from food moisture.
These adequate intakes apply only to conditions of moderate environmental temperature and moderate physical activity levels (PAL = 1.6).

checks.label: Water a day this week, from Food (ml)
checks.basis: EFSA: "2.0 L/day" for women and "2.5 L/day" for men, total water "from drinking water, beverages of all kind, and from food moisture"

not_said: Counted from what you log in Food, foods and drinks alike; a day with nothing logged in Food is not counted.
EFSA's figures assume "moderate environmental temperature and moderate physical activity levels".
The figure follows the sex in your profile; with none set, nothing is compared.

cards.name: Blood pressure at home

says.text: At home: two readings a minute or more apart, sitting down, morning and evening, for at least 4 days and ideally 7. The first day's readings are left out and the rest averaged.
High blood pressure is confirmed by a clinic reading of 140/90 or higher together with a home average of 135/85 or higher.
135/85 or higher when checked at home

sources.title: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management (NG136)

checks.label: Home average, last 7 days, first day left out (mmHg)
checks.basis: NICE NG136 1.2.7–1.2.8: a home average of 135/85 or higher

not_said: A home average is not a diagnosis: NICE also asks for a clinic reading of 140/90 or higher.
Treatment targets are agreed with a clinician; the app sets none.

cards.name: Your cycle

says.by: FIGO System 1, as restated by Jain, Munro and Critchley 2023 (CC BY)
says.text: The number of days in an average menstrual cycle from the first day of bleeding in one cycle to the first day of the next cycle. The normal length of a menstrual cycle ranges from 24 to 38 days, whereas abnormal frequency of menstruation is less than 24 days (frequent menses) or more than 38 days (infrequent menses).

…the count begins with the onset of bleeding and ends on the last day of blood flow, including the light bleeding, often called spotting. It is normal for women to bleed for up to eight consecutive days

…below the age of 18 and after 45 years, ovulatory disorders are frequent and norms are not well defined. For women aged 18–25 years and those 42–45 years of age, cycle length can vary by up to 9 days. For those aged 26–41 years, the range is smaller—up to 7 days.
All the metrics are based on the previous 6 months, provided there has been no pregnancy or puerperium.
…ranging from every 21 days to every 35 days… Your period can last between 2 and 7 days
Bleeding between periods, bleeding after having sex, or bleeding after the menopause needs to be checked by a doctor.
Using an app or a diary to keep track of your periods can help you see if they're irregular. Day 1 of your menstrual cycle is the first day of your period.

cards.disagree: FIGO counts 24 to 38 days as the normal length of a cycle and the NHS 21 to 35; FIGO counts up to 8 days of bleeding and the NHS 2 to 7. Each is shown with its name, never blended.

sources.by: FIGO (Jain, Munro, Critchley, Int J Gynecol Obstet 2023)
sources.title: FIGO's Abnormal Uterine Bleeding System 1, restated

checks.label: Cycles of the last 6 months, in days
checks.basis: FIGO: "ranges from 24 to 38 days"

checks.label: The same cycles
checks.basis: NHS: "every 21 days to every 35 days"

checks.label: Days of bleeding in a row, latest period
checks.basis: FIGO: "up to eight consecutive days", spotting included

checks.label: The same days
checks.basis: NHS: "between 2 and 7 days"

checks.label: Longest cycle less the shortest
checks.basis: FIGO: "can vary by up to 9 days" at 18–25 and 42–45, "up to 7 days" at 26–41

checks.label: Days of spotting with no period, last 6 months
checks.basis: NHS: "Bleeding between periods … needs to be checked by a doctor"

not_said: Nothing is predicted: not the next period, not fertile days, not ovulation, and nothing is read from a late period.
The app does not call a cycle irregular; it shows each body's numbers beside yours.
A cycle that overlaps a context you set (contraception, pregnancy, after a birth, perimenopause), or that you marked as missed logging, is left out, and says so.
Where you live, a local GP or clinic is the place for the NHS's advice.

cards.name: Heavy periods

says.text: Heavy menstrual bleeding is defined by what it does to someone's life (physically, socially, emotionally or materially), not by an amount of blood.
Treatment should aim to improve that, rather than to reduce a measured loss.

need to change your pad or tampon every 1 to 2 hours…; need to use 2 types of period product together…; have periods lasting more than 7 days; pass blood clots larger than about 2.5cm (the size of a 10p coin); bleed through to your clothes or bedding; avoid daily activities…; feel tired or short of breath a lot

heavy periods are affecting your life; you've had heavy periods for some time; you have severe pain during your periods; you bleed between periods or after sex; you have heavy periods and other symptoms, such as pain when peeing, pooing or having sex

sources.title: Heavy menstrual bleeding: assessment and management (NG88)

checks.label: Days at heavy flow, latest period
checks.basis: NICE NG88: heavy is defined by what it does to your life, not by an amount

checks.label: Days of bleeding in a row, latest period
checks.basis: NHS: "have periods lasting more than 7 days"

not_said: It does not diagnose heavy menstrual bleeding.
It does not work out a blood loss in millilitres, nor a pictorial chart score: there is no agreed cut-off for one (Magnay 2020).

cards.name: Periods and migraine

says.text: Occurring exclusively on day 1 ± 2 (ie, days −2 to +3) of menstruation in at least two out of three menstrual cycles and at no other times of the cycle.
…in at least two out of three menstrual cycles, and additionally at other times of the cycle.
The first day of menstruation is day 1 and the preceding day is day −1; there is no day 0.
For research purposes a prospective diary is recommended, but this is not mandatory for clinical diagnosis
Migraine linked to periods is diagnosed with a headache diary kept for at least 2 menstrual cycles.

sources.title: ICHD-3, A1.1.1 Pure menstrual migraine without aura

checks.label: Of your last 3 periods, with a headache on days −2 to +3
checks.basis: ICHD-3: "day 1 ± 2 (ie, days −2 to +3) … in at least two out of three menstrual cycles"

not_said: It does not name a type of migraine: ICHD-3 also asks that the attacks meet its criteria for migraine without aura, which a diary of severity cannot show.
It is a count to bring to a clinician, as NICE asks.

cards.name: Premenstrual symptoms

urgent.text: Call 999 or go to A&E if: you have symptoms of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) and are feeling suicidal

says.text: keep a diary of your symptoms for at least 2 menstrual cycles – you can take this to a GP appointment
lifestyle changes have not helped; your symptoms are affecting your daily life

says.by: DSM-5-TR, PMDD criterion F, as reproduced in Naik et al. 2023 (CC BY)
says.text: Criterion A should be confirmed by prospective daily ratings during at least two symptomatic cycles.

checks.label: Cycles of the last 6 months with a diary entry every day
checks.basis: NHS: "for at least 2 menstrual cycles"

not_said: It never says PMDD, "meets criteria" or "likely": that is a clinician's to say.
Track the symptoms you have as your own (＋ in Diary); the card counts the cycles your diary covers.
999 is the UK's number; in Singapore, 995 and mindline 1771 are above. Where you live, use your own.

cards.name: Mood (PHQ-9)

says.text: PHQ-9 Depression Severity. This is calculated by assigning scores of 0, 1, 2, and 3, to the response categories of "not at all," "several days," "more than half the days," and "nearly every day," respectively.
Scores of 5, 10, 15, and 20 represent cutpoints for mild, moderate, moderately severe and severe depression, respectively.
…a final decision about the actual risk of self-harm requires a clinical interview.
Risk tools and scales should not be used to predict suicide or self-harm.

sources.title: PHQ screeners: "no permission is required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute them"
Self-harm: assessment, management and preventing recurrence (NG225)

form.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following:

items.text: Little interest or pleasure in doing things?
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much?
Feeling tired or having little energy?
Feeling bad about yourself—or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down?
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television?
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed? Or the opposite—being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual?
Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way?

checks.label: PHQ-9 total, latest
checks.basis: PHQ-9 instructions: 0 to 3 for each answer, added; 0 to 27

not_said: A score is not a diagnosis, and the app does not name one.
It does not judge or predict risk: NICE says scales must not be used to predict self-harm.
If the last question is not "Not at all", the contacts above are for now, and a clinician is for soon.

cards.name: Activity and mood

says.text: Planning activities and doing them (behavioural activation) helped with low mood across many trials, and it also helped when people did it on their own, though less.
Delivered by junior workers with little training, behavioural activation did as well as cognitive behavioural therapy.
Behavioural activation looks at the link between what a person does and how they feel.
Self-help works about as well alone as with support when symptoms are mild; when they are more than mild, help from someone does better at first.

sources.by: Cuijpers et al., Clin Psychol Rev 2026
sources.title: Behavioural activation for depression: meta-analysis
Depression in adults: treatment and management (NG222)

checks.label: Days this week you did something you planned
checks.basis: Behavioural activation: plan something, do it, and note how it felt

not_said: It is not treatment, and it is not a substitute for help when low mood lasts.
If keeping this makes you feel worse, stop or take a break: in one trial, people who rated their mood daily did not do better.
Nothing you write is scored or judged.

cards.name: Writing it down

says.text: Writing about what has been hard has a small effect on wellbeing, on average.
Any benefit tends to come later, not right away, and is larger with a few days between sessions.

says.by: Pennebaker and Beall 1986 (from a secondary source)
says.text: Straight after writing, people often feel worse for a while.

sources.title: Experimental disclosure and its moderators: a meta-analysis

not_said: Nothing you write is read, scored or judged by the app.
Expect to feel worse right after writing; stop when you need to.
Your journal is the Timeline; a Writing note is one entry, kept on the Mind shelf.
